newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes off, Canada imports mulled.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes off, Canada imports mulled.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices eased with benchmark grades Wednesday, but the discount market held as refiners waiting to see if extra Canadian crude would come west after a three-day pipeline shutdown.
Canada's IPL Energy Inc said Wednesday all its pipelines stretching into Midwestern U.S. resumed pumping and full power was expected soon at pumping stations shut by a weekend storm.
West Coast traders waited to see if IPL would announce shipping restrictions on Midwest deliveries in order to handle resurgent volumes.
Any restrictions could force crude to the U.S. West Coast.
But early indications showed little increased demand on Canada's pipeline into the Pacific Northwest, officials said.
"I haven't seen any producers panicking yet," one Canadian trader said.
"When (IPL) knows what they can run...then they'll make an announcement," one trader said, noting that apportionments could be announced as early as Friday.
West Coast refiners hoped extra Canadian supplies would be sold at a strong discount.
Meanwhile, West Coast crude buyers were angered by a rumor that BP secretly sold a second cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude last week at a discount wider than $1.05, the current posted price.
BP and Exxon denied selling the cargo, but U.S. Oil, the alleged buyer, declined to comment when asked if they purchased the crude.
Outright ANS fell 10 cents to $18.53/18.73 a barrel.
Texaco will take delivery of a 400,000 barrel South Blend cargo into Anacortes, Washington, May 20, traders said, and is trying to sell part of the cargo.
A 2,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) shipment for California heavy grade in May sold at postings Tuesday, traders said.
